diagnosis: Complicated crown-root fractures of maxillary central incisors 11 and 21 secondary to road traffic accident, with Ellis Class VIII traumatic injury pattern, pulp exposure, Grade II mobility, subgingival oblique crown-root fracture extension, poor crown-root ratio, loss of ferrule effect, and hopeless restorative prognosis.
treatmentProvided: Atraumatic extraction of non-restorable teeth 11 and 21 was performed under local anesthesia using periotomes and extraction forceps with preservation of surrounding alveolar bone. Sockets were curetted, debrided, and irrigated with normal saline. After healing and bone assessment, two 3.75 mm x 13 mm endosseous implants were placed in regions 11 and 21 with primary stability greater than 35 Ncm. Cover screws were placed and flaps sutured with 3-0 silk. After osseointegration, healing abutments were placed, impressions were made, and implant-supported zirconia crowns were fabricated and delivered after esthetic, phonetic, and occlusal verification.
treatmentPlan: Atraumatic extraction of teeth 11 and 21, socket preservation and debridement, healing period with bone-quality assessment, placement of two endosseous implants in regions 11 and 21, healing abutment placement after osseointegration, fabrication and cementation of implant-supported zirconia crowns, and periodic follow-up with peri-implant maintenance. Patient was informed that root canal treatment and post-core restoration had poor prognosis because of extensive crown-root fracture and inadequate remaining tooth structure. Informed consent was obtained.
dietAdvice: Soft diet during immediate post-extraction and post-implant healing periods.
Avoid biting directly with the anterior implant region until definitive prosthesis delivery.
Maintain meticulous oral hygiene around surgical and prosthetic sites.
Report pain, swelling, bleeding, implant mobility, prosthesis loosening, or discharge immediately.
notes: Extraoral findings: mild swelling and tenderness of upper lip with superficial abrasions; no evident facial bone fracture.

Intraoral findings: Ellis Class VIII traumatic injury involving teeth 11 and 21, approximately three-fourths clinical crown fracture of both teeth, pulp exposure, Grade II mobility, gingival laceration, cervical bleeding, and positive percussion tenderness.
Both teeth showed poor crown-root ratio and inadequate remaining tooth structure for post and core restoration.

Pre-operative IOPA: extensive coronal destruction of teeth 11 and 21, oblique crown-root fractures extending subgingivally, widened periodontal ligament space, loss of ferrule effect, poor endodontic-restorative prognosis, intact surrounding alveolar bone, and adequate bone volume for future implant placement.

Post-operative radiograph: complete removal of fractured teeth, proper implant positioning in regions 11 and 21, adequate crestal bone levels, good implant parallelism, absence of peri-implant radiolucency, and successful osseointegration with stable bone support.
Outcome: complete relief from pain with restored function, improved esthetics, speech, and masticatory efficiency.
Follow-up at 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months showed satisfactory healing and stable implant-supported restorations.
Prognosis: excellent because of adequate bone support, successful osseointegration, favorable implant positioning, and good oral hygiene maintenance.
